newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Mar 10.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Mar 10.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Senior Telstra officials said yesterday the national carrier is on track to provide the Howard Government with a Budget windfall in the form of a one-off dividend payment, or capital repayment, of up to A$3 billion, a figure which will help bring down the"headline" Budget deficit, as part of its preparations for partial privatisation. Page 1.

The Australian Labor Party has revealed it will now vote for Government legislation aimed at allowing the controversial Hindmarsh Bridge in South Australia to proceed when the Bill returns to the Senate. The decision reflects the ALP's efforts to differentiate itself from the Howard Government by dumping hardline economic and Aboriginal affairs policies to appeal to the tradition "battlers" constituency. Page 3.

Federal Opposition Spokesman on Aboriginal Affairs Daryl Melham said yesterday he had several legal opinions that a High Court challenge against the Coalition's Hindmarsh Bridge legislation could also wipe out of contention several of the legislative optins being considered following the controversial Wik native title decision. Page 3.

The Australian Securities Commission claims an advertisement for emu farming group Flightless Birds of Australia, which ran on radio station 2UE in Sydney, breached the Corporations Law because it gave an overly optimistic picture of the security and potetial returns of the investment and was likely to mislead potential investors. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Following a telephone call on Friday to Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer from his Papua New Guinea counterpart Kilroy Genia, assuring that no mercenaries would be utilised in Bougainville, Prime Minister John Howard held a secret meeting with PNGPrime Minister Sir Julius Chan yesterday on the Bougainville crisis. Page 1.

Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett said yesterday he would like to send the unions an "invoice" for the losses incurred from a 26 per cent drop in attendance at the Australian Formula One Grand Prix, which Kennett blames on a two-day strike by transport workes. He predicted the loss in attendance cost taxpayers A$5 - 10 million. Page 1.

According to an independent study which has been presented to the Federal Government, Federal politicians face a punitive tax of up to 44 per cent on the large superannuation payouts because of a flaw in the Budget surcharge on super. The study confirms te A$500 million-a-year Budget super tax is flawed because the real rate of tax actually increases the longer the politicians stay in Parliament. Page 1.

Speaking at a weekend conference hosted by the conservative Samuel Griffith Society in Canberra, Former High Court Chief Justice Sir Harry Gibbs described the Wik decision as unsatisfactory and signalled his support for Federal Legislation to overturn thecontroversial decision. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Under a plan called the Limited Service Volunteers Scheme, being pushed within the bureaucracy for further development by Cabinet's Employment Committee, the young unemployed would be given the option of doing rudimentary military training at army camps t help improve their motivational skills. Page 1.

Under a new system of non-union individual work contracts called Australian Workplace Agreements, companies will be able to cash-out of workers' entitlements such as sick leave and long service leave and will be able to bypass union involvement for the fist time. Page 1.

Just days before the release of the New South Wales Government's report on the future of the Higher School Certificate, State Education Minister John Aquilina has revealed departmental analysis confirms the need to make the HSC fairer by reforming the curiculum. The data shows many students are discouraged from tackling the toughest courses. Page 1.

A prospective investment boom in rural New South Wales will be highlighted to ministers today as they travel to Tamworth to prepare for a critical country Cabinet meeting tomorrow. Projects worth A$11.5 billion and with the potential to create 32,700 jobsin the bush are being planned by Australian and international businesses. Page 3.
THE AGE

Following the weekend strike by 9,500 tram, train and bus staff, Victorian Transport Minister Robin Cooper yesterday withdrew the Government's offer of a six per cent pay rise and a reform agreement and the State Government refused to rule out selling the entire public transport system or standing down staff amid tension with unions over reform. Page A1.

Papua New Guinea Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan, who is under international pressure over hiring African-based mercenaries as part of a plan to ease the fighting on Bougainville, has attended crisis talks in Sydney with Prime Minister John Howard, during hich Howard reiterated Australia's strong opposition to the plan. Page A1.

Despite criticisms of a transport strike at yesterday's Grand Prix in Melbourne, many of the 107,000 racegoers who attended were united in their praise for the staging of the event, particularly the use of 600 buses to carry people to and from the city. Pge A1.

Following last month's media allegations of drug abuse and violence in Government residential units for children in care, key welfare professionals have warned against the move to privatise the care of Victoria's most abused and neglected children, with some claiming the State Government is trying to avoid responsibility for the troubled child protection system. Page A2.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
